Hacking a "secure" AI agent operating system - OpenFang
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6ghATZc0w1g
I tried the responsible disclosure route, but since the maintainers have been completely unresponsive both over email and on X, here's some 0day for you to enjoy :) From OpenFang's README: "16 Security Systems Defense in Depth OpenFang doesn't bolt security on after the fact. Every layer is independently testable and operates without a single point of failure." Code https://github.com/RightNow-AI/openfang Site https://openfang.sh For this RCE, neither of those 16 security systems were of any use. And looking closer at the security systems in question, it turns out they weren't even doing what they were supposed to do anyway _(ツ)_/ The "taint tracking" used to enforce an allowlist of commands for agents could be trivially bypassed in at least four different ways (command-splitting on , ;, && and but a whitelisted command followed by & cmd, cmd, (cmd) and newlinecmd works fine. Overall, they're fighting a losing game by implementing a command line parsing based sandbox rather than using an actual sandbox (using seccomp-bpf, for instance), a container or a microVM As for the AES-256-GCM based auth in the OpenFang P2P protocol, well, besides being vulnerable to a replay attack, the protocol itself is completely in plaintext after the handshake! Regarding the "WASM sandboxes", turns out they aren't actually used for anything, there's not a single WASM agent in the repo, and since rather than conforming to WASI they require implementing a completely custom API, it's unlikely that anyone would bother making a WASM based agent in the first place (not even the maintainers do, so) And as for the "Merkle audit trail", that audit trail is stored entirely in-memory, so simply restarting the daemon is enough to erase any traces of that trail Anyway, enjoy the RCE PoC!
